subject: Speeding up HTML document opening in Terminal Delight based on measured renderer delays
reader: Parker built Terminal Delight and asked for faster Alt+O and artifact opening. He knows the product, but has not seen the renderer measurements or the GPU startup failure.

sections.heading: Opening Speed
sections.text: Opening a brief should feel immediate. The renderer reproduced your two-second wait, and an existing graphics option cut it substantially—but made the first open worse.

sections.heading: 01 The Wait
sections.text:
A recent glass brief took 2.35 seconds to fill the visible area of the page, called its viewport. Reading the file and notes cost less than a millisecond. Capturing the page into pictures consumed most of the delay. TD already keeps its browser running between opens, saves completed page images and draws the visible area first. Vulkan, an alternative graphics mode already supported by TD, made those captures faster. 
 01 · A Faster Capture 

 Faster capture gets close to a fourfold improvement on this page. Medians of three; the Vulkan median hides the cold-start problem below. 
Measured with the actual renderer, 968 × 1400 CSS pixels at 1.6 scale. Includes sequential capture/decode; excludes browser startup and native display. Method and limits .

sections.heading: 02 The First Open
sections.text:
Starting a fresh Vulkan browser produced a 6.2–8.3 second first viewport . Later opens fell to about 0.6 seconds. That penalty repeated, so simply enabling Vulkan would make some opens much worse. 
 | 
 | Measured page | Current | Vulkan | Gain 
 | Formal verification | 2.35 s | 0.65 s | 3.6× 
 | Desktop contention | 2.13 s | 0.60 s | 3.5× 
 | Agent identity | 2.30 s | 0.83 s | 2.8× 
 | 26.5 MB chalk study | 2.66 s | 1.94 s | 1.4× 

Per-page medians of three. Raw current samples , Vulkan samples and fresh-browser repeat . The large image-heavy page spends more time loading; no universal fourfold gain is established.

sections.heading: 03 Before the Click
sections.text:
A completed render already reads from the cache in 1–6 milliseconds . Decoding and putting it on screen still take time, but this gives prepared opens a credible route toward 10×. TD knows the newest declared artifact before you open it. 
 02 · Prepare the Next Brief 

 Preparation can move the expensive capture ahead of opening. Proposed mechanism; its native speed and background cost are unmeasured. 

Limit preparation to one cancellable job for the newest handover. Keep the existing cache budget. A changed file, local asset or frame size must invalidate reuse. This trades some background work for a faster click; it needs a responsiveness and memory check.

sections.heading: 04 The Build
sections.text:
I recommend one implementation pass: measure from pressing Alt+O to seeing the page, make capture cheaper without a worse first open, then prepare the newest artifact. Target 4× for ordinary opens and 200–300 ms for prepared opens . The latter is the 10× ambition, still to be proven. 

The verification includes actual pixels, note positions, keyboard navigation, edits, resized frames and cancelled opens. The graphics mode’s startup must improve before it becomes the default. A large new document opened immediately remains a separate case. 

 Approve this combined implementation plan? The technical plan names the interfaces, slices and acceptance tests. Production code, application preferences and your running window are unchanged. 

Difficulty 6/10: one approval under the software-factory skill . Investigation and reproducible measurements are complete. Implementation awaits that approval. 

Evidence: measurement summary · source-backed probe · continuation state · measurement decision .
